Task: Deduplicate Report Query OrderBy Construction in Supports Module

  • Area: Supports / Admin / Deduplication / Clean Architecture
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/SupportResponse.go
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/SupportResponse_test.go
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/ListReportPost.go
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/ListReportComment.go
    • src/Action/V1/Supports/ListReportUser.go
  • Date: 29-10-2026

1. Problem & Context

Across multiple administrative support report handlers (ListReportPost.go, ListReportComment.go, and ListReportUser.go), parsing sort query parameters (created and total) and constructing SQL ORDER BY clauses was repeated identically:

  • Parsing createdSort (oldest -> ASC, else DESC).
  • Parsing totalSort (most -> DESC, least -> ASC, else omitted).
  • Constructing slice orderBy and joining with , .
    This resulted in 20+ lines of duplicate logic copy-pasted across 3 separate files.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Centralized OrderBy Helper (src/Action/V1/Supports/SupportResponse.go):
    • Implemented buildReportOrderBy(alias, createdQuery, totalQuery string) string.
    • Encapsulates parameter normalization and returns the exact sanitized SQL ORDER BY clause.
  2. Controller Refactoring:
    • Replaced duplicate sort parsing and slice construction in ListReportPost.go, ListReportComment.go, and ListReportUser.go with single-line calls to buildReportOrderBy.
  3. Zero Configuration & Zero Contract Changes:
    • Database ordering and API response payloads remain 100% identical.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Added unit test table TestBuildReportOrderBy covering default sorting, oldest created, most total reports, and least total + oldest combinations in SupportResponse_test.go.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • 50+ lines of duplicate query sorting logic eliminated.
  • SQL ORDER BY behavior remains 100% identical.
  • 100% unit tests pass in src/Action/V1/Supports.
  • Clean build and vet checks.

issues.display_title: Issue #603: Centralize Response Encryption Envelope Boilerplate
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Response Encryption Envelope Boilerplate

  • Date: 30-10-2026
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Configuration: ZERO NEW ENV REQUIRED

1. Summary

Deduplicated and standardized response encryption boilerplate across 60+ controller endpoints:

  1. Centralized Helpers (src/Utils/Functions/response.go):

    • Added SendJSONOrEncrypted to dispatch either plaintext JSON or encrypted envelope (cry, ls, extras).
    • Added SendJSONOrEncryptedPayload to preserve handlers where inner encrypted payload differed from plaintext response.
    • Added EncryptedExtras to bundle "messages" and conditional "e4": encrypt for viewer role.

  2. Controller Refactoring Across 16 Packages:

Task: Centralize Response Encryption Envelope Boilerplate

  • Area: Core Architecture / Controllers / Response / Clean Code / Deduplication
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Utils/Functions/response.go
    • src/Utils/Functions/response_test.go
    • 60+ controllers across src/Action/V1/* and src/Action/V2/* (Affiliate, Bookmarks, Broadcast, Categories, CollectionPost, Comments, Hashtag, Likes, MentionPosts, Notifications, Places, Posts, Recommendations, Search, Users, V2/Posts)
  • Date: 30-10-2026

1. Problem & Context

Across 60+ endpoint controllers in panorra-api-go, the response encryption logic was copy-pasted with identical boilerplate:

if ec == "true" {
    encText := Functions.EncryptSuccessResult(responses, lastLogin, encrypt)
    responses = map[string]interface{}{
        "messages": "...",
        "cry":      encText,
        "ls":       Functions.EpochTime(lastLogin),
    }
    if role == "viewer" {
        responses["e4"] = encrypt
    }
}
return c.Status(fiber.StatusOK).JSON(responses)

This repetitive 10-15 line block appeared over 65 times throughout the codebase, creating substantial maintenance overhead and boilerplate noise.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Centralized Response Dispatcher (src/Utils/Functions/response.go):
    • Implemented SendJSONOrEncrypted(c, response, lastLogin, encrypt, shouldEncrypt, extras...):
      • Returns HTTP 200 with plaintext JSON if shouldEncrypt == false.
      • Returns HTTP 200 with encrypted envelope (cry, ls, plus optional extras) if shouldEncrypt == true.
    • Implemented SendJSONOrEncryptedPayload(c, response, payloadToEncrypt, lastLogin, encrypt, shouldEncrypt, extras...):
      • Allows handlers where the encrypted payload differs from the unencrypted response (e.g. inner res, dataList, or suggestionUser) to maintain 100% byte-for-byte fidelity.
    • Implemented EncryptedExtras(messages, role, encrypt):
      • Automatically attaches "messages": messages and injects "e4": encrypt only when role == "viewer".
  2. Controller Refactoring:
    • Replaced duplicate encryption blocks across 60+ controller handlers with standardized Functions.SendJSONOrEncrypted / Functions.SendJSONOrEncryptedPayload calls.
    • Completely preserved slim endpoint handling and *Slim.go files without modification.
  3. Zero Configuration & Zero Breaking Changes:
    • 100% backward compatible: status codes, plaintext JSON models, encrypted envelope keys (messages/message, cry, ls, e4), and encryption mechanisms are completely identical.
    • ZERO new environment variables required.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Added unit test suite in src/Utils/Functions/response_test.go verifying plain JSON delivery, encrypted envelope composition, inner payload preservation, and viewer-role e4 injection.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • 500+ lines of duplicate encryption boilerplate eliminated across 60+ controllers.
  • 100% identical response structures (both plain JSON and encrypted envelope).
  • All unit tests pass across all packages (go test ./...).
  • Clean go vet and go build ./cmd/... checks.
